questions.question: Two transversal lines S and T cut a set of distinct parallel lines. S cuts the parallel lines in points A, B, C and D and T cuts the parallel lines in points E, F, G and H. If AB = 5 cm, CD = 3 cm and EF = 15 cm, then the length (in cm) of GH is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Intercept Theorem** states that parallel lines cut any two transversals in the same **ratio**.

Ratio of segments on transversal **S** = Ratio of segments on transversal **T**

AB ÷ CD = EF ÷ GH

5 ÷ 3 = 15 ÷ GH

GH = (3 × 15) ÷ 5 = 9 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 9 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of segment **AB = 5 cm**

Length of segment **CD = 3 cm**

Length of segment **EF = 15 cm**

**Formula Used:**

According to the **Intercept Theorem** (or **Thales Theorem** for parallel lines), if three or more parallel lines intersect two transversals, then they cut off the transversals **proportionally**.

AB ÷ EF = BC ÷ FG = CD ÷ GH

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b512c6990fabfb240542d90e619ca866291d3c7d177f28b80f88b4aeef8886cc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ AB ÷ EF = CD ÷ GH

⇒ 5 ÷ 15 = 3 ÷ GH

⇒ 1 ÷ 3 = 3 ÷ GH

⇒ GH = 3 × 3

⇒ GH = 9 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 9 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Intercept Theorem

If three or more parallel lines are intersected by two transversals, the segments cut off on one transversal are proportional to the corresponding segments on the other.

Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT)

Also known as Thales Theorem, it states that a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio.

Parallel Lines and Transversals

The distance between parallel lines remains constant, but the length of the transversal segment increases as the angle of the transversal with the parallel lines decreases.</p

questions.question: In an isosceles triangle, the vertex angle measures 14°. What is the measure of each of the base angles?
questions.solution: __Shortcut Trick__ In an **isosceles triangle**, the two **base angles** are always **equal**. Base Angle = (180° − **Vertex Angle**) ÷ 2 Base Angle = (180° − 14°) ÷ 2 Base Angle = 166° ÷ 2 = 83° **∴ The correct answer is 83° and 83°.** **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** **Vertex angle** of the **isosceles triangle** = 14° **Formula Used:** Sum of all **interior angles** of a triangle = 180° [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0411c2b2fa02e6fca0f322dcf73cc0ff0a77fd2ce817cf3fd9fc7e296729b69.png] **Calculations:** ⇒ Let the measure of each **base angle** be x. ⇒ Since it is an **isosceles triangle**, the two base angles are equal. ⇒ 14° + x + x = 180° ⇒ 14° + 2x = 180° ⇒ 2x = 180° − 14° ⇒ 2x = 166° ⇒ x = 166° ÷ 2 ⇒ x = 83° **∴ The correct answer is 83° and 83°.** **__Additional Information__** Isosceles Triangle Theorem If two sides of a triangle are **congruent**, then the angles opposite those sides (base angles) are also **congruent**.

questions.question: If an angle of a parallelogram is 27° less than four-fifth of its adjacent angle, then find the smallest angle of the parallelogram.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **adjacent angles** in a **parallelogram** is always 180°.

Let the **adjacent angle** be x.

x + (4/5 × x − 27°) = 180°

9/5 × x = 207°

x = 115°

Smallest angle = 180° − 115° = 65°.

**∴ The correct answer is 65°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

One angle = 4/5 × (**adjacent angle**) − 27°

**Formula Used:**

In a **parallelogram**, the sum of any two **adjacent angles** is 180° (**supplementary angles**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c0d73bda1a092c6cc30e5d4ef052efe9599c463f9467ec2115cb212d4941643.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **adjacent angle** be A.

Let the other angle be B.

⇒ B = (4/5)A − 27

⇒ A + B = 180 (Sum of **adjacent angles**)

⇒ A + (4/5)A − 27 = 180

⇒ (9/5)A = 180 + 27

⇒ (9/5)A = 207

⇒ A = (207 × 5) ÷ 9

⇒ A = 23 × 5 = 115°

⇒ B = 180° − 115° = 65°

Comparing 115° and 65°, the **smallest angle** is 65°.

**∴ The correct answer is 65°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Parallelogram

Opposite sides are **parallel** and **equal** in length. Opposite angles are **equal**, and **consecutive angles** are **supplementary** (sum to 180°).

Diagonals of a Parallelogram

The **diagonals** of a **parallelogram** bisect each other, meaning they cut each other into two equal parts at their point of intersection.

Area of a Parallelogram

The **area** is calculated as Base × Height, or using **trigonometry** as a × b × sin(θ), where a and b are adjacent sides and θ is the included angle.</p

Sum of **interior angles** = 100% more than 360° = 2 × 360° = 720°.

Using the formula (n − 2) × 180° = 720° ⇒ n − 2 = 4 ⇒ n = 6.

The polygon is a **regular hexagon**.

Each interior angle x = 720° ÷ 6 = 120°.

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

⇒ Sum of interior angles = 360° + (100/100) × 360° = 720°

⇒ n − 2 = 4

⇒ n = 6 (The polygon is a **regular hexagon**)

⇒ Each interior angle x = 720° ÷ 6 = 120°

**∴ The correct answer is 120.**

questions.question: The larger of two supplementary angles is 62° more than the smaller one. The smaller angle (in degree) is:
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Sum of two **supplementary angles** = 180° Difference between the angles = 62° **Smaller angle** = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 **Smaller angle** = (180° − 62°) ÷ 2 = 118° ÷ 2 = 59° **∴ The correct answer is 59°.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** Larger angle = Smaller angle + 62° Sum of **supplementary angles** = 180° **Formula Used:** If two angles are supplementary, their sum is 180°. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e9abeca962921169dc2204c6e747fe9d4b73528d71b0928b066bddc4605602e8.png] **Calculations:** ⇒ Let the **smaller angle** be x. ⇒ Then the **larger angle** = x + 62°. ⇒ Since they are **supplementary**, x + (x + 62°) = 180° ⇒ 2x + 62° = 180° ⇒ 2x = 180° − 62° ⇒ 2x = 118° ⇒ x = 59° **∴ The correct answer is 59°.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE if PQRS is a rectangle?

options.text: The diagonals of rectangle PQRS do not bisect each other

questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

A **rectangle** is a special type of parallelogram where all four angles are right angles (90°).

By the properties of a parallelogram, the diagonals of a rectangle **always bisect each other**.

Therefore, the statement 'The diagonals of rectangle PQRS do not bisect each other' is mathematically **FALSE**.

**∴ The correct answer is The diagonals of rectangle PQRS do not bisect each other.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

PQRS is a **rectangle**.

**Properties of a Rectangle:**

1. Opposite sides are equal and parallel: PQ = RS and PS = QR.

2. All four interior angles are equal to 90°: ∠P = ∠Q = ∠R = ∠S = 90°.

3. Diagonals are equal in length: PR = SQ.

4. Diagonals bisect each other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c4546a2838f36837d6a521482b9ad963d6b08fff5a9a420ba42a3720ed80d053.png] 

Let us analyze each option based on the properties of a rectangle:

⇒ **Option 1:** ∠P = ∠Q = ∠R = ∠S = 90°. This is **TRUE** because by definition, all angles of a rectangle are right angles.

⇒ **Option 3:** Diagonal PR = Diagonal SQ. This is **TRUE** because the diagonals of a rectangle are always equal in length.

⇒ **Option 4:** PQ = RS and PS = QR. This is **TRUE** because a rectangle is a parallelogram, and opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal.

⇒ **Option 2:** The diagonals of rectangle PQRS do not bisect each other. This is **FALSE** because a rectangle is a parallelogram, and the diagonals of any parallelogram (and thus any rectangle) must bisect each other (i.e., PO = OR and SO = OQ).

⇒ Therefore, the false statement is Option 2.

**∴ The correct answer is The diagonals of rectangle PQRS do not bisect each other.**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of Diagonals in Quadrilaterals

In a **parallelogram**, diagonals bisect each other. In a **rectangle**, diagonals bisect each other and are equal. In a **rhombus**, diagonals bisect each other perpendicularly. In a **square**, diagonals bisect each other perpendicularly and are equal.

Area and Perimeter of a Rectangle

For a rectangle with length l and width w, the **Area** = l × w, and the **Perimeter** = 2 × (l + w).

Diagonal Length Formula

The length of the diagonal d of a rectangle with sides a and b is given by the Pythagorean theorem: d = √(a² + b²).</p

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of quadrilateral?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

A **quadrilateral** is defined as a polygon with exactly **four sides**.

A **trapezoid**, **rhombus**, and **kite** are all 4-sided polygons, which makes them types of quadrilaterals.

An **octagon** is an 8-sided polygon, so it is **NOT** a quadrilateral.

**∴ The correct answer is Octagon.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A list of geometric shapes to classify based on the number of sides.

**Concept:**

Polygons are classified according to the number of sides they possess:

⇒ **Quadrilateral:** 4 sides

⇒ **Octagon:** 8 sides

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8806b7baa97001daad393361d374a070b463d548c1bdba21d46920d8e0e30596.png] 

**Calculations and Analysis:**

⇒ **Trapezoid:** Has 4 sides (Quadrilateral).

⇒ **Rhombus:** Has 4 equal sides (Quadrilateral).

⇒ **Kite:** Has 4 sides with two pairs of equal adjacent sides (Quadrilateral).

⇒ **Octagon:** Has 8 sides.

⇒ Therefore, the octagon does not belong to the quadrilateral family.

**∴ The correct answer is Octagon.**

**__Additional Information__**

Types of Quadrilaterals

Common quadrilaterals include squares, rectangles, parallelograms, rhombuses, trapezoids, and kites. The sum of their interior angles is always 360°.

Sum of Interior Angles Formula

The sum of the interior angles of any n-sided polygon is given by (n − 2) × 180°. For an octagon (n = 8), the sum of the interior angles is 1080°.

Polygon Classification

Polygons are named based on their number of sides: Triangle (3), Quadrilateral (4), Pentagon (5), Hexagon (6), Heptagon (7), Octagon (8), Nonagon (9), Decagon (10).</p

questions.question: Let ABC and DEF be two triangles such that ∠A = ∠D = 40° and AB = DE. What is the condition required to be met such that ABC and DEF are similar triangles?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two triangles to be **similar**, their corresponding angles must be equal according to the **AA (Angle-Angle) Similarity Criterion**.

Given: ∠A = ∠D = 40°.

To satisfy similarity, we need at least one more pair of **corresponding angles** to be equal.

From the options, **∠C = ∠F** provides the necessary second pair of equal corresponding angles.

Since ∠A = ∠D and ∠C = ∠F, the triangles **ΔABC** and **ΔDEF** are similar by **AA similarity**.

**∴ The correct answer is ∠C = ∠F.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** In ΔABC and ΔDEF, ∠A = ∠D = 40° and AB = DE.

**Formula Used:** **AA Similarity Criterion** — If two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another triangle, then the triangles are similar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c0bfacfb0bc7286d060fe586757976d96fd52130c04692afe71670144cbfcb0.png] 

To prove ΔABC ~ ΔDEF:

⇒ We already have one pair of equal angles: ∠A = ∠D = 40°.

⇒ According to the **AA Similarity Criterion**, we need another pair of corresponding angles to be equal.

⇒ The corresponding vertices are A → D, B → E, and C → F.

⇒ Therefore, either **∠B = ∠E** or **∠C = ∠F** must be true.

⇒ Checking the options, **∠C = ∠F** is provided in option (1).

⇒ Note: Since AB = DE is also given, if ∠C = ∠F, then ∠B = ∠E (angle sum property), making the triangles **congruent** by **ASA**. Since all congruent triangles are similar, the condition is satisfied.

**∴ The correct answer is ∠C = ∠F.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

AA Similarity Criterion

If two angles of one triangle are respectively equal to two angles of another triangle, then the two triangles are similar.

SAS Similarity Criterion

If one angle of a triangle is equal to one angle of another triangle and the sides including these angles are proportional, then the triangles are similar.

Similarity vs Congruence

Congruent triangles have the same shape and size (ratio of sides = 1), while similar triangles have the same shape but may differ in size (ratio of sides is constant).</p

questions.question: The ratio of the lengths of two corresponding sides of two similar triangles is 10 : 9. The ratio of the areas of these two triangles, in the order mentioned, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any two **similar triangles**, the ratio of their **areas** is equal to the **square** of the ratio of their **corresponding sides**.

Ratio of corresponding sides = 10 : 9

⇒ Ratio of areas = 10² : 9²

⇒ Ratio of areas = 100 : 81

**∴ The correct answer is 100 : 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of the lengths of two **corresponding sides** of two **similar triangles** = 10 : 9

**Formula Used:**

If ΔABC ∼ ΔPQR, then:

Area(ΔABC) / Area(ΔPQR) = (AB / PQ)² = (BC / QR)² = (AC / PR)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea3ba7417e32f72dfa9573167b4ce0fa4ff486f71d8be2f1b78860cab6765591.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **corresponding sides** of the two triangles be s₁ and s₂.

⇒ s₁ / s₂ = 10 / 9

Let the **areas** of the two triangles be A₁ and A₂.

According to the **Area of Similar Triangles Theorem**:

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = (s₁ / s₂)²

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = (10 / 9)²

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = (10 × 10) / (9 × 9)

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = 100 / 81

⇒ A₁ : A₂ = 100 : 81

**∴ The correct answer is 100 : 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio of Perimeters

For two **similar triangles**, the ratio of their **perimeters** is equal to the ratio of their **corresponding sides** (s₁ : s₂).

Ratio of Altitudes and Medians

The ratio of **corresponding altitudes**, **medians**, or **angle bisectors** of two **similar triangles** is also equal to the ratio of their **corresponding sides**.

Conditions for Similarity

Two triangles are **similar** if their **corresponding angles** are equal (AAA) or their **corresponding sides** are in the same ratio (SSS or SAS).</p

questions.question: AB is a chord in the minor segment of a circle of centre Q. P is a point on the major arc AB. The tangents drawn from external point D to the circle are AD and BD. If ∠APB = 39°, then find the measure of ∠ADB.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The angle subtended by a chord at the **center** is twice the angle subtended at the **major arc**: ∠AQB = 2 × ∠APB.

In a circle, the angle between two **tangents** from an external point and the angle subtended by the chord of contact at the center are **supplementary**.

⇒ ∠ADB = 180° − ∠AQB

⇒ ∠ADB = 180° − (2 × 39°) = 180° − 78° = 102°.

**∴ The correct answer is 102°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠APB = 39°, **Q** is the center, **AD** and **BD** are tangents from external point **D**.

**Formula Used:** ∠Center = 2 × ∠Circumference; Sum of angles in quadrilateral = 360°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ccc9f8d9398efa0d97b79c415df95d30a1885e3ab396c00506a6025fd6293a7f.png] 

⇒ The angle subtended by chord **AB** at the center **Q** is twice the angle at point **P** on the major arc.

⇒ ∠AQB = 2 × ∠APB = 2 × 39° = 78°

⇒ In quadrilateral **AQBD**, the radii **QA** and **QB** are perpendicular to tangents **AD** and **BD** respectively.

⇒ ∠QAD = 90° and ∠QBD = 90°

⇒ Sum of angles in **AQBD** = 360°

⇒ ∠AQB + ∠QAD + ∠QBD + ∠ADB = 360°

⇒ 78° + 90° + 90° + ∠ADB = 360°

⇒ 258° + ∠ADB = 360°

⇒ ∠ADB = 360° − 258° = 102°

**∴ The correct answer is 102°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle at Center Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center of a circle is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Tangent-Radius Property

A tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact (∠Radius, Tangent = 90°).

Tangent Quadrilateral

In a quadrilateral formed by two radii and two tangents from an external point, the opposite angles at the center and the external point are supplementary (sum = 180°).</p

questions.question: The number of diagonals in a regular octagon is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The number of diagonals in any polygon with **n** sides is given by the direct formula:

**Number of diagonals = n × (n − 3) ÷ 2**

For a regular octagon, the number of sides is **n = 8**.

⇒ Number of diagonals = 8 × (8 − 3) ÷ 2

⇒ Number of diagonals = 8 × 5 ÷ 2 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20 diagonals.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A regular octagon has **8 vertices** (n = 8) and **8 sides**.

**Formula Used:**

The number of diagonals is the total number of lines that can be drawn by connecting any two vertices, minus the number of boundary sides:

**Number of diagonals = ⁿC₂ − n**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/079f4ea6ab3665811d71522c317b285c2e1d8138cfa5152eb48d17bd13cf6270.png] 

**Calculations:**

The total number of ways to choose 2 vertices out of 8 is given by ⁸C₂:

⇒ ⁸C₂ = (8 × 7) ÷ (2 × 1)

⇒ ⁸C₂ = 28 lines

These 28 lines include both the boundary sides of the octagon and its internal diagonals.

Subtracting the 8 boundary sides of the octagon:

⇒ Number of diagonals = 28 − 8

⇒ Number of diagonals = 20

**Option Analysis:**

__
 
• **Option (1) - 19:** Incorrect. A polygon with 19 diagonals would have a non-integer number of sides, as solving n(n − 3) ÷ 2 = 19 yields no integer solution.
 
• **Option (2) - 20:** Correct. As calculated, an octagon (8 sides) has exactly 20 diagonals.
 
• **Option (3) - 21:** Incorrect. A heptagon (7 sides) has 14 diagonals, and an octagon has 20. No regular polygon has exactly 21 diagonals.
 
• **Option (4) - 24:** Incorrect. A nonagon (9 sides) has 27 diagonals. No regular polygon has exactly 24 diagonals.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 diagonals.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

General Formula for Diagonals

The number of diagonals in any n-sided polygon is given by the formula: d = n(n − 3) ÷ 2.

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of an n-sided polygon is (n − 2) × 180°. For an octagon, this is (8 − 2) × 180° = 1080°.

Each Interior Angle of a Regular Octagon

Each interior angle of a regular octagon is 1080° ÷ 8 = 135°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

The sum of the exterior angles of any polygon is always 360°. For a regular octagon, each exterior angle is 360° ÷ 8 = 45°.</p

questions.question: For a regular polygon, the sum of the interior angles is 300% more than the sum of its exterior angles. Each interior angle of the polygon measures x°. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **sum of exterior angles** of any regular polygon is always **360°**.

The **sum of interior angles** is 300% more than the sum of exterior angles:

⇒ Sum of interior angles = 360° + 300% of 360° = 4 × 360° = **1440°**

Number of sides (n) = (Sum of interior angles ÷ 180°) + 2 = (1440° ÷ 180°) + 2 = **10**

Each interior angle (x) = Sum of interior angles ÷ n = 1440° ÷ 10 = **144°**

**∴ The correct answer is 144°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The sum of the interior angles of a **regular polygon** is 300% more than the sum of its exterior angles.

Each interior angle of the polygon measures **x°**.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of exterior angles of any polygon = **360°**

Sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon = **(n − 2) × 180°**

Each interior angle of a regular polygon = **[(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/19d27f57ff5ea0f884f4b0058ea258ad33abe6f62e8194ff50a7b11f4f2950c2.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the number of sides of the regular polygon be **n**.

The sum of the exterior angles of any polygon is always 360°.

⇒ Sum of exterior angles = 360°

According to the question, the sum of the interior angles is 300% more than the sum of its exterior angles:

⇒ Sum of interior angles = Sum of exterior angles + 300% of Sum of exterior angles

⇒ Sum of interior angles = 360° + (300 ÷ 100) × 360°

⇒ Sum of interior angles = 360° + 3 × 360°

⇒ Sum of interior angles = 4 × 360° = 1440°

Using the formula for the sum of interior angles:

⇒ (n − 2) × 180° = 1440°

⇒ n − 2 = 1440° ÷ 180°

⇒ n − 2 = 8

⇒ n = 10

Thus, the polygon has **10 sides** (it is a **regular decagon**).

Now, each interior angle (x) of a regular polygon with 10 sides is:

⇒ x = Sum of interior angles ÷ n

⇒ x = 1440° ÷ 10

⇒ x = 144°

**Option Analysis:**

**Option (1) 140:** If each interior angle is 140°, then each exterior angle is 180° − 140° = 40°. The number of sides would be 360° ÷ 40° = 9. For a nonagon, the sum of interior angles is 7 × 180° = 1260°, which is 250% more than 360° (not 300%). Thus, this option is incorrect.

**Option (3) 134:** If each interior angle is 134°, the number of sides is not an integer (360° ÷ 46° ≈ 7.83), which is impossible for a regular polygon. Thus, this option is incorrect.

**Option (4) 156:** If each interior angle is 156°, the number of sides is not an integer (360° ÷ 24° = 15, which gives a sum of interior angles of 13 × 180° = 2340°, which is 550% more than 360°). Thus, this option is incorrect.

**∴ The correct answer is 144°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of an n-sided polygon is always equal to (n − 2) × 180°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

The sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon is always constant and equal to 360°, regardless of the number of sides.

Relationship between Interior and Exterior Angles

At each vertex of a polygon, the interior angle and the exterior angle are supplementary, meaning their sum is always 180°.

Number of Diagonals

The total number of diagonals in an n-sided polygon is given by the formula: [n × (n − 3)] ÷ 2.</p

The sum of all exterior angles of any regular polygon is always **360°**.

Sum of interior angles = 360° + 50% of 360° = 360° + 180° = **540°**.

The polygon with a sum of interior angles equal to 540° is a regular **pentagon** (5 sides).

Each interior angle (x) of a regular pentagon = 540° ÷ 5 = **108°**.

**∴ The correct answer is 108°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Sum of interior angles = Sum of exterior angles + 50% of Sum of exterior angles

Each interior angle = x°

**Formula Used:**

Sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon = (n − 2) × 180°

Sum of exterior angles of any polygon = 360°

Each interior angle of a regular polygon = [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n

We know that the sum of the interior angles of an n-sided polygon is given by the formula:

⇒ (n − 2) × 180° = 540°

⇒ n − 2 = 540° ÷ 180°

⇒ n − 2 = 3

⇒ n = 5

Thus, the polygon is a regular **pentagon** (n = 5).

Each interior angle of a regular polygon is given by:

⇒ x = [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n

⇒ x = (3 × 180°) ÷ 5

⇒ x = 540° ÷ 5

⇒ x = 108°

**Why other options are incorrect:**

⇒ **Option (4) 88°:** If each interior angle is 88°, then the number of sides n = 360° ÷ (180° − 88°) = 360° ÷ 92° = 3.91, which is not an integer.

**∴ The correct answer is 108°.**

The angle formed by the **external bisectors** of two angles of a triangle is given by the formula:

Given ∠A = 84°

∠P = 90° − 84°/2 = 90° − 42° = 48°

**∴ The correct answer is 48°.**

∠A = 84°

**Formula Used:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/afc752c40eddfa6c38369cbc191acce463263c0cf45579765241c44cbd13f463.png]

⇒ In **▵ABC**, the sides AB and AC are produced to points D and E respectively.

⇒ The bisectors of **exterior angles** ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at point P.

⇒ Point P is the **ex-center** of the triangle opposite to vertex A.

⇒ The measure of ∠P is given by the relation: ∠P = 90° − ∠A/2

⇒ Substituting the value of ∠A = 84°:

⇒ ∠P = 90° − (84° / 2)

⇒ ∠P = 90° − 42°

⇒ ∠P = 48°

**∴ The correct answer is 48°.**

questions.question: In ΔABC, DE ∥ AC, where D and E are the points on sides AB and BC, respectively. If BD = 2 cm and AD = 19 cm, then what is the ratio of the area of ΔBDE to the trapezium ADEC?

Area of **trapezium ADEC** = Area(ΔBAC) − Area(ΔBDE) = 441 − 4 = 437.

Required ratio = Area(ΔBDE) : Area(trapezium ADEC) = 4 : 437.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 437.**

⇒ Let Area(ΔBDE) = 4k and Area(ΔBAC) = 441k.

⇒ Area of **trapezium ADEC** = Area(ΔBAC) − Area(ΔBDE) = 441k − 4k = 437k.

⇒ Ratio of Area(ΔBDE) to Area(trapezium ADEC) = 4k : 437k = 4 : 437.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 437.**

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio: BD/DA = BE/EC.
